prompt:
A test sled operates on a straight rail track during an emergency braking and reverse test. Forward is defined as the positive direction.

[FIGURE PLACEHOLDER: Velocity-time graph for a test sled from t = 0 to t = 16.0 s. Vertical axis: velocity v in m s^-1, scale from -8.0 to +12.0. Horizontal axis: time t in s, scale from 0 to 16.0. The graph has five straight segments: (1) from (0, 0) to (4.0, +10.0); (2) horizontal line at v = +10.0 m s^-1 from t = 4.0 s to t = 8.0 s; (3) line from (8.0, +10.0) passing through (10.0, 0) to (12.0, -6.0); (4) horizontal line at v = -6.0 m s^-1 from t = 12.0 s to t = 14.0 s; (5) line from (14.0, -6.0) to (16.0, 0).]

(a) Identify the time at which the sled reaches its maximum forward displacement from its starting position, and calculate this maximum displacement. [2]
(b) Calculate the resultant displacement of the sled at the end of the 16.0 s test. [2]
(c) Calculate:
  (i) the average velocity of the sled over the full 16.0 s test; [1]
  (ii) the average speed of the sled over the full 16.0 s test. [1]

response_structure.description: Time of maximum displacement and calculation of maximum displacement

hints: Maximum forward displacement occurs at the instant velocity crosses from positive to negative (turning point).
Calculate the area above the time axis up to this turning point.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: The sled moves forward as long as v > 0. It reaches its furthest forward point when v becomes 0 at t = 10.0 s.
Step 2: Region from 0 to 10.0 s is a trapezium: base = 10.0 s, top = 8.0 - 4.0 = 4.0 s, height = 10.0 m s^-1.
common_pitfalls: Assuming maximum displacement occurs at the end of the test (t = 16.0 s).
Choosing t = 8.0 s where deceleration begins rather than t = 10.0 s where velocity reaches zero.

hints: Calculate the negative area under the time axis from t = 10.0 s to t = 16.0 s.
Add the negative area to the maximum forward displacement.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: Negative region from 10.0 s to 16.0 s is a trapezium below the axis: base = 16.0 - 10.0 = 6.0 s, top = 14.0 - 12.0 = 2.0 s, height = -6.0 m s^-1.
Step 3: Resultant displacement = +70.0 m + (-24.0 m) = +46.0 m.
common_pitfalls: Adding 24.0 m instead of subtracting it for displacement.
Miscalculating the duration of the horizontal reverse segment.

hints: Average velocity = resultant displacement / total time.
Average speed = total distance / total time.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: Average velocity = +46.0 m / 16.0 s = +2.88 m s^-1.
Step 2: Total distance = 70.0 m + 24.0 m = 94.0 m.
Step 3: Average speed = 94.0 m / 16.0 s = 5.88 m s^-1.
common_pitfalls: Using distance to calculate average velocity.
Using displacement to calculate average speed.

hints: The sled reaches its furthest forward point when velocity drops to zero.
Combine forward and reverse areas for displacement; add magnitudes for total distance.
solution:
(a) Maximum displacement occurs at t = 10.0 s (turning point where v = 0). Maximum displacement = 0.5 x (10.0 + 4.0) x 10.0 = +70.0 m.
(b) Reverse area (10.0 to 16.0 s) = 0.5 x (6.0 + 2.0) x (-6.0) = -24.0 m. Resultant displacement = +70.0 - 24.0 = +46.0 m.
(c)(i) Average velocity = +46.0 m / 16.0 s = +2.88 m s^-1.
(c)(ii) Total distance = 70.0 + 24.0 = 94.0 m. Average speed = 94.0 m / 16.0 s = 5.88 m s^-1.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: Identify that velocity is positive until t = 10.0 s, so maximum forward position is at t = 10.0 s.
Step 2: Calculate positive area: 0.5 x (10.0 + 4.0) x 10.0 = +70.0 m.
Step 3: Calculate negative area: 0.5 x (6.0 + 2.0) x (-6.0) = -24.0 m.
Step 4: Resultant displacement at t = 16.0 s = +70.0 - 24.0 = +46.0 m.
Step 6: Total distance = 70.0 + 24.0 = 94.0 m; average speed = 94.0 / 16.0 = 5.88 m s^-1.

mark_scheme.criterion: States t = 10.0 s as the time of maximum displacement
Calculates reverse area: 0.5 x (6.0 + 2.0) x (-6.0) = -24.0 m
